recent_posts.title: Built an API dev tool and got 11k+ installs already, this is what happened since we open sourced.
recent_posts.summary: Voiden is an offline, file-based API client built as a Postman replacement that has reached 11k installs since open sourcing. API requests are composed from reusable blocks (endpoint, auth, params, body) stored as plain executable markdown (.void files), enabling Git-based collaboration and versioning. Key lessons from open sourcing include community PRs driving product direction, tighter feedback loops, and the natural fit of versioning API requests like code. Recent additions include API workflow scripting (JS/Python/Shell), a plugin SDK, and an AI integration layer for tools like Claude and Codex to operate on .void files.

recent_posts.title: OpenSail: open-source workspace for agentic software work
recent_posts.summary: OpenSail is an open-source workspace designed for agentic software development, positioning itself as a free alternative to closed-source tools like Codex App, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Cowork. The project is available on GitHub under the TesslateAI organization.

recent_posts.title: Two APIs, One Platform: How OpenChoreo Separates Developer Experience from Platform Governance
recent_posts.summary: OpenChoreo addresses the classic developer platform tension between developer freedom and platform governance by exposing two distinct API surfaces. Developers work with application-level abstractions (Projects, Components, Workloads, WorkflowRuns) without needing to understand Kubernetes internals. Platform engineers work with infrastructure-level abstractions (ComponentTypes, Traits, Environments, DeploymentPipelines, DataPlanes) to define policies and constraints. The control plane translates developer intent into infrastructure resources governed by platform engineer configuration. ComponentType is the key composition point — developers reference a type defined by platform engineers, which determines what they can configure, what traits are available, and what Kubernetes resources get generated. The model allows platform engineers to enforce policies (like NetworkPolicies via Cilium) without developer involvement, while developers can deploy without filing tickets or writing Kubernetes manifests.

recent_posts.title: Why open source is quietly winning platform engineering
recent_posts.summary: Open source tooling is quietly dominating platform engineering, with teams composing CNCF-backed projects like Backstage, Argo CD, Flux, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Cilium, and KEDA into internal developer platforms (IDPs). The argument is that this approach wins because the code is auditable, community-driven improvements outpace vendor roadmaps, and teams avoid lock-in. The post predicts the next wave will be opinionated reference implementations that compose this ecosystem without replacing it. OpenChoreo, a CNCF Sandbox project, is highlighted as an example of this pattern — composing the same open source stack into a production-ready IDP.

recent_posts.title: OpenChoreo: The Open Source Internal Developer Platform That Gets the Plane Architecture Right
recent_posts.summary: OpenChoreo is an open source Internal Developer Platform (IDP) built around a four-plane architecture: Control Plane (API server, controllers, AI agents via Flux/GitOps), Workflow Plane (Argo Workflows, Cloud Native Buildpacks, pluggable CI/CD), Data Plane (workload isolation, KEDA scaling, Cilium/Kubewarden security, kgateway), and Observability Plane (OpenSearch, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry). Cross-cutting concerns like auth (OAuth2/OIDC), secret management (ESO-compatible), and container registries are all pluggable. A notable feature is first-class AI Agent Modules (SRE, FinOps, Architect agents) embedded in the Control Plane, alongside an Observer MCP in the Observability Plane, positioning OpenChoreo for agentic platform operations.

recent_posts.title: If you need secure your ssh server then use onuion-sshd AI Agent.
recent_posts.summary: onuion-sshd is an AI-powered SSH security agent that integrates with Linux PAM to perform real-time risk scoring on login attempts. It analyzes session history, calculates risk scores using the onuion model, and automatically blocks high-risk IPs via iptables. It runs as a systemd daemon, supports JSON logging for SIEM integration, and uses a fail-open policy to avoid locking out legitimate users. Installation is via a shell script, with PAM configuration requiring a single line addition.

recent_posts.title: State Inconsistency in Fee Accounting: When Ordering Becomes an Attack Surface
recent_posts.summary: A deep dive into how improper ordering of state updates in fee accounting systems can create exploitable vulnerabilities. When economic invariants are not explicitly defined and enforced, systems can silently break their own math — passing tests and audits while remaining fundamentally compromised. The post explores how operation ordering becomes an attack surface in fee-related state transitions.

recent_posts.title: ros2_info
recent_posts.summary: ros2_info is an open source fetch/info tool for ROS2 environments that consolidates environment information into a single view, eliminating the need to switch between multiple terminals during development. Created by Gaurav Shah, it targets ROS2 developers looking to streamline their workflow.

recent_posts.title: Open First, Monetize Later: The Risks and Realities
recent_posts.summary: A reflection on the recurring pattern of open-source projects shifting licenses or introducing commercial gating once they achieve mass adoption and face business pressure. Using examples like Terraform/OpenTofu, Redis/Valkey, and Elastic/OpenSearch, the author argues that 'open first, monetize later' is a risky strategy. The most durable open-source tools tend to be built by companies where the tool is not the primary revenue driver. The post advocates for honesty early on: either commit to genuine long-term open infrastructure, or build a commercial product with clear incentives from the start — mixing the two causes most of the ecosystem pain.

recent_posts.title: Developer Friction as a Service (DFaaS). Better acronyms?
recent_posts.summary: A short hot take arguing that developer tools like Insomnia and Postman have followed a pattern of introducing account requirements and paywalls, creating friction that developers resent. The prediction is that developers will eventually abandon any tool that forces cloud lock-in, as monetization pressures inevitably erode the frictionless early experience that made those tools popular in the first place.

top_posts.summary: Cascader-Shadcn is a new open-source cascading dropdown component for Shadcn UI that provides hierarchical menu navigation with click or hover expansion. It supports icons, custom labels, and per-option disabling, offering similar functionality to Ant Design and React Suite cascaders in a lightweight, Shadcn-compatible package.
